query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor boron addition into the eutectic high-entropy alloy will result in boron segregation at the internal lamellar boundaries, thereby enhancing interfacial cohesion and delaying microcrack nucleation. This modification is expected to simultaneously improve both tensile strength and ductility at room temperature.
generation.material_initial_state: An as‐cast eutectic high‐entropy alloy displaying dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries that are prone to microcrack initiation during tensile deformation.
generation.intervention: Incorporate a small amount of boron (e.g., approximately 0.1–0.5 at.%) during alloy melting so that boron segregates to the lamellar interfaces during solidification and subsequent homogenization heat treatment.
generation.conditions: Samples are produced by conventional casting followed by a homogenization heat treatment. Room-temperature tensile tests are performed in ambient air at quasi‐static strain rates to match the typical deformation conditions of the baseline alloy.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced interfacial cohesion at the dual-phase lamellar colony boundaries due to boron segregation, which minimizes localized embrittlement and delays microcrack initiation.
generation.mechanism: Boron atoms have a propensity to segregate to high-energy interfaces. Their presence at the lamellar boundaries reduces the local stress concentration and mitigates microcrack initiation during tensile loading. This interfacial strengthening also helps to retard crack propagation, thereby enabling increased strain hardening while maintaining or enhancing the overall strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: The boron-modified alloy is predicted to exhibit higher tensile strength and increased elongation (ductility) relative to the unmodified lamellar baseline due to reduced microcracking and improved interfacial performance.
generation.baseline: The unmodified eutectic high-entropy alloy exhibits high strength but limited ductility at room temperature, primarily as a result of microcrack initiation at the numerous internal boundaries between the dual-phase lamellae.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective provided that the boron addition promotes segregation rather than forming deleterious boride phases. Its efficacy depends on careful control of the boron content and processing conditions to ensure that the beneficial segregation occurs without altering the overall lamellar structure detrimentally.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal boron concentration and processing parameters required to achieve the desired interfacial segregation and mechanical improvements are not fully defined. Additionally, quantitative improvements must be verified, as excessive boron or inappropriate heat treatment could lead to unwanted phase formation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloys using identical casting and heat treatment procedures: one set with the specified minor boron addition and one baseline set without boron. Conduct detailed microstructural analysis using TEM/SEM coupled with compositional mapping (e.g., EDS) to confirm boron segregation at the lamellar boundaries. Perform room-temperature tensile tests at quasi-static strain rates to compare mechanical properties.
measurements: Microcrack density and fracture surface morphology
Elemental segregation profiles at phase boundaries (via TEM/EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-modified alloys fail to show statistically significant improvements in both tensile strength and elongation relative to the baseline, or if microstructural analysis does not confirm boron segregation at the internal boundaries, then the hypothesis is falsified.
